name: main.js
summary: Main frontend entry point handling authentication, file upload, data visualization, dataset management, and chat interface
purpose: Serves as the central client-side controller that orchestrates user interactions across authentication, dashboard data rendering, file uploads, and real-time chat, providing a unified interface for the application
responsibilities: Initialize and manage authentication flows (login and register forms)
Handle file uploads via drag-and-drop and file input controls
Render data visualizations using Chart.js across multiple canvas contexts
Manage dataset visibility state (show and hide active datasets)
Provide chat interface functionality including sending messages and rendering chat bubbles
Dynamically render tabular data with generated headers and rows
Coordinate with imported API and animation utility modules
inputs: User interactions including form submissions, button clicks, file drops, and chat messages
DOM references such as forms, canvas contexts, table containers, and chat containers
Backend data responses passed through the API module
outputs: Updated DOM with rendered charts, tables, chat bubbles, and dataset views
API calls triggered through the imported api module
Animated UI transitions triggered through the imported animations module
File upload payloads transmitted to the backend
architecture_notes: Acts as a monolithic frontend controller mixing authentication, dashboard, chat, and visualization concerns in a single vanilla JavaScript module. It relies on direct DOM manipulation and imperative scripting rather than a component-based framework, importing only peripheral utilities for API communication and animations. The high density of mixed responsibilities and DOM references indicates a 'god script' anti-pattern that centralizes the entire application lifecycle
improvements: Decompose into feature-specific modules (e.g., auth.js, dashboard.js, chat.js, charts.js) to separate concerns
Adopt a component-based architecture or lightweight frontend framework to encapsulate UI sections
Extract DOM querying and manipulation into dedicated view or controller classes
Introduce a centralized state management pattern instead of scattered global variables
Move chart configuration and table rendering logic into reusable service or presenter modules
Add per-feature error handling boundaries rather than relying on a single shared error element
